+### Residual Plans And Runtime Monitors
+
+Follow the complete protocol in
+[Residual Checks And Runtime Trace Monitors](../../../etas-core/docs/architect/etas-residual-checks-design.md)
+and its [implementation work list](../../../etas-frontend/docs/architect/residual-checks-implementation-worklist.md).
+Use `plan/residual/{validate,bind,coverage}.rs` for actual artifact-producing
+passes, not facade wrappers. Their inputs are frontend-verified neutral plans;
+their output is complete checked-site/scope/provider coverage and engine-owned
+installation evidence. Both ordinary preparation and CandidatePublisher require
+this gate. Descriptive runtime_checks, a configured PolicyClient or an unchecked
+boolean cannot authorize a callable.
+
+`etas_code::residual` supplies one pure monitor kernel backed by Utils automata.
+Use `eval/residual/{scope,event,step,exit,evidence}.rs` as its typed engine adapter
+and `control/residual/{state,permit}.rs` for live state/single-dispatch permits.
+Do not reimplement clause semantics in eval or Host. Prepared revisions share
+immutable plans/factories; each invocation activates bounded independent scope
+instances while retaining outer restrictions across calls and revision bridges.
+
+CheckedActionInvocation, perform/default forwarding, handler continuations and
+the explicit machine supply typed semantic events. Observe source-handled
+requests as well as default Host execution; do not monitor only external I/O.
+Attempts, handled/default dispatch and actual completion are distinct phases.
+Validate predicates and current evidence before governed dispatch, then correlate
+outcomes. Pending/denied/failed approval is not accepted evidence, and a dry-run
+handler is not a successful external write. Keep whole OR alternatives and exact
+scope/correlation keys. No stale permit, unordered action set or log-string
+matching may bypass checks; do not hold monitor locks across Host awaits.
+
+Normal/tail/non-local return, Error propagation, finish, abort/never and cancel
+all visit scope exit. Validate scope acceptance before releasing a normal
+result; `A << B` requires prior B and adds no eventual-action requirement.
+Preserve primary failure/cancellation plus incomplete obligations
+on abnormal exit, without automatic compensation or retry. Yield, suspension
+and checkpoint creation are not exits. Parent scopes settle children before
+final acceptance; parallel decisions have one explicit scope-owned ordering.
+
+Checkpoint codecs preserve plan/revision/contract identities, historical progress/
+register bindings, pending outcomes, cursor and scope ownership consistently
+with machine state. Restore uses current authority and explicitly invalidates
+old run-local approvals, permits and approval-dependent Approved/armed readiness.
+Preserve other progress, denied branches and confirmed outcomes; do not reset
+the whole monitor or trust a saved flag. Missing/malformed state or an unsafe
+evidence-lifetime transition rejects. Historical replay cannot mint fresh
+approval or dispatch an event twice. Unknown completion remains unknown.
+Optional cross-run reuse requires an application-enabled verifying provider,
+not ordinary checkpoint storage. Enforcement is independent of trace export,
+profiling and sampling. Existing budget/sandbox guards remain in force.

+### 11.1 Text Values, Lazy Sequences, And Typed Errors
+
+Implement [chapter 19](../../../etas/docs/design/19-standard-library.md#1-strings-and-text-apis)
+using the existing `etas_std`, `etas_builtin`, `etas_types` and interpreter
+crate. No new text/iterator crate, Host service, Unicode backend in the
+evaluator, or text-only execution pipeline is introduced.
+
+Reuse these boundaries and split their files by responsibility when needed:
+
+| Existing boundary | Responsibility |
+|---|---|
+| `value/text.rs` | Immutable shared `StringValue`, borrowed access, alias-preserving storage updates |
+| `value/iteration.rs` / its `iteration/` children | Generic sequence descriptor and per-consumer cursor; text is one supported sequence family |
+| `intrinsic/pure/abi/text.rs` | Borrowed text/bytes projection and typed scalar/tuple/segment/sequence outputs |
+| `intrinsic/pure/abi/result.rs` and checked variant projection | Correct `Option`, `Result`, `TextError` and `Normalization` identities |
+| Existing plan dispatch / checked iterable tables | Bind the resolved std operation and exact item/result types once |
+| Existing machine loop frames / safe points | Advance the cursor, bind the item and preserve progress across yield/control flow |
+| Existing checkpoint value/frame codecs and validators | Validate and restore sequence source/recipe/cursor without native pointers |
+
+The engine-owned `SequenceValue` retains immutable source/configuration and a
+checked sequence kind/item type. For text it wraps the neutral recipe defined
+by [builtin text kernels](../../../etas-core/docs/architect/etas-builtin-design.md#10-text-kernels-and-lazy-sequences).
+It does not contain a shared mutable iterator. Each `for` creates its own cursor
+and advances via the shared kernel; two loops over one value and nested loops
+are independent. Source updates cannot change a retained iteration snapshot.
+Use the same iterable dispatch as collections, not one evaluator branch per
+`std.text` function name. This does not add a public `next` method absent from
+the SPEC.
+
+`chars`, `char_indices`, `lines`, `split_iter`, `split_whitespace`, `find_all`,
+`graphemes` and `grapheme_indices` must not first allocate an `Array`. Create the
+recipe without scanning or copying the whole retained input; only consumed
+elements are projected. `split` and `splitn` deliberately return eager arrays
+and share the same scanner's segmentation rules. The current
+`TextOutput::Array` adapter may remain for these eager outputs, never as a
+fallback for a checked `Iter<T>` result. Loop progression saves scanner state
+instead of repeatedly restarting at byte zero.
+
+Passing input strings to a kernel borrows `StringValue::as_ref()` rather than
+cloning into owned `BuiltinValue::String`. Retain immutable backing across
+suspension; short returned segments may copy or share storage according to the
+storage policy. Zero-copy slicing is not a language guarantee. Keep the existing
+COW/owned-buffer optimizations and ensure edits never mutate an observed alias.
+Do not introduce a source-visible builder, mutable string receiver or special
+assignment pattern to implement these APIs. Bulk join/concat reuse the shared
+checked-size assembly kernel, not repeated concatenation in the ABI adapter.
+
+Checked text failures enter the normal `Error<TextError>` effect/handler
+machinery at the call's real source span. `?` captures that effect. Parsing and
+formatting instead return checked `Result::Err` variants; optional access returns
+`None`. Remove any adapter that turns parser errors into arbitrary strings,
+all invalid access into IndexError, resource failure into TextError, or a missing
+operation into an empty result. `std.codec.text` keeps `TextCodecError` and its
+explicit Reject/Replace policy. The receiver/output ABI must not erase nominal
+identity by accepting any string-shaped wrapper.
+
+Long native scans, normalization, formatting and large output growth cooperate
+with the existing work budget, cancellation and safe-point scheduler through
+bounded kernel work. An interrupt cannot expose a partial immutable result.
+Preflight representable sizes, enforce limits before/while growing, and retain
+the existing resource-exhaustion channel rather than inventing a recoverable
+TextError for every allocation failure. Empty-pattern progress, UTF-8 boundary
+validation and concrete numeric widths are kernel contracts, not engine patches.
+
+When a checkpoint includes a lazy value or active text loop, save the immutable
+source/configuration, operation discriminator, cursor phase/progress, checked
+item type and text/Unicode compatibility fingerprint. Validate source size,
+offsets, phase, boundaries and operation-specific state under current restore
+limits before use. Do not serialize Rust borrowed iterators, an OS handle,
+pointer or all remaining elements. Resume preserves the exact next element and
+does not re-execute previously completed loop actions. Incompatible cursor/ABI
+versions are rejected explicitly, not silently restarted or coerced to arrays.
+Ordinary Host value encoding does not gain an implicit iterable-to-array
+conversion; only a separately declared checked boundary can require one.
 
+Tests cover all chapter 19 families end-to-end, independent/nested consumers,
+early break without unvisited allocations, iteration across handler suspension,
+checkpoint/resume at empty-pattern and line boundaries, forged cursor rejection,
+Unicode version mismatch, exact errors and cancellation during a large scan.
+Use the existing allocation/operation-counter harness to verify linear traversal
+and bulk assembly. Native kernels and ordinary std bodies share conformance
+vectors; passing only a Rust helper test is not source/API completion evidence.

 Calling an agent:

-Writer.ask(input)

-executes:
+executes the selected revision's method body. An explicit infer site performs:
 
 ```text
-evaluate agent body/context harness -> Prompt
-Prompt + model config + tools + authority -> ModelRequest
+evaluate infer argument -> Prompt
+Prompt + current agent method identity/config/tools/authority -> ModelRequest
 HostServices::model(request) -> ModelResponse
-decode/validate response -> declared output type
+decode/validate response -> infer output O
+continue ordinary method control flow -> method result
 ```
 
-Multi-step orchestration, approval gates, persistent memory writes, and
-post-output validation remain ordinary `flow` code around the agent call.
+Methods can perform zero, one or multiple inference operations. Record
+Agentic.infer<C, O> at those explicit sites, where C is the selected method;

+Surrounding flows normally own business orchestration, while intentionally
+included method behavior remains checked by its actual public contract.
 
+### Reflection And Pinned Executable Revisions
+
+SPEC chapter 18 adds bounded reflection and checked agent/ordinary-flow revisions.
+Reading ^current uses the implementation carried by that value, not always the
+source declaration. AgentDef<A> compiles to nominal A; CallableDef<F> compiles
+to the original ordinary callable type F with its checked generic/escaping-row
+bindings. Bare CallableDef and direct agent-method descriptors remain read-only.
+current = candidate changes one binding and leaves old aliases/active calls
+unchanged.
+
+Replace the assumption that AgentItem(HirItemId) alone identifies an executable.
+Use an engine-owned ExecutableRevision reference containing shared checked
+program/prepared plan, stable agent/method/free-flow identity, target family/A/F
+interface, generic instantiation, revision/contract/dependency
+fingerprints, required type relocation, retained definition leases and installed
+residual checks. Static and compiled values use revision-aware targets; do not
+convert free flows to fake agents or require a public run-code wrapper.
+
+Use value/code/{definition,agent,callable}.rs, plan/code/, eval/reflection.rs,
+eval/code/execution.rs,
+driver/dispatch/compiler.rs and api/code/publisher.rs. CandidatePublisher uses
+the ordinary interpreter planning pipeline and must not run the candidate.
+Do not introduce an interpreter-local checker, eval(string), a pseudo-AIR or
+fallback to the original agent/flow when candidate validation fails. CallableDef<F>
+projects one-way to an erased metadata value using checked projection facts;
+runtime signature strings or an expected return type cannot recover F.
+
+Use an explicit RevisionTypeBridge for nominal inputs/outputs/higher-order values:
+HirItemId/TypeId are local to a checked program. Matching runtime value shapes
+cannot substitute for checked stable type/constructor identity.
+
+Ordinary flow calls select the pinned revision using existing higher-order call
+dispatch. Preserve latent summary/frozen callable provenance through assignment,
+parameters, returns and type bridges; a callable's escaping row is not its full
+requested-action/trace contract. A pure compiled F may be invoked without compiler
+authority, but producing it still performs Code.compile and execution remains
+subject to its current ordinary authority/handler/trace/limit boundaries.
+
+The caller's source was checked against C_frozen before dynamic candidate
+compilation; no precise candidate-body summary is required at that stage.
+Compilation derives a fresh S_new, validates it against that same authoritative
+contract and installs residual enforcement before publishing A/F. Return a
+revision-bound value containing matching target/interface, contract, dependency/
+configuration identities and S_new. Validate custom-handler-supplied callables
+against the same contract; matching F or nominal A alone is insufficient.
+
+Keep contract-bound caller facts and actual revision analysis separate. Do not
+patch the running caller's checked facts after compilation. ^candidate exposes
+S_new while subsequent with_body/compile preserves C_frozen rather than replacing
+it with the narrower or wider inferred summary of the latest body. Missing or
+mismatched provenance rejects; original implementation substitution is not a
+recovery path. See the
+[static-to-runtime handoff protocol](../../../etas-frontend/docs/architect/etas-reflection-design.md#static-contract-facts-and-runtime-summary-handoff).
+
+Pure parse/format/with_body/diff use injected in-memory CodeSyntaxOperations;
+Code.check/compile go through normal scoped/default handlers, requested actions,
+authority, trace, cancellation and budgets. Compilation does not execute model/
+tool code and compiler permission does not grant candidate permissions.
+
+Checkpoint/replay pin target family, A/F, executable revision/contract/environment
+and relocation identities and validate them on restore. Missing/tampered state
+fails explicitly, never selects an original declaration. Private engine snapshots
+are not a public binary code-loader API. Public persistence saves source plus
+locked surrounding definitions/contract/dependency/config identities; restoration
+uses statically typed reflection, fingerprint validation, parse/with_body/compile
+under current authority/limits. Stored summaries or erased descriptors are not
+proof and cannot recover F. No implicit mutable-path source recompilation occurs
+during reflection or invocation.
+
+CodeSyntaxOperations and compiler work inherit active limits/cancellation;
+WallTime includes service wait. Revisions/retries cannot refresh allowances.
+CPU/memory ceilings use service-configured duration/byte units, not model tokens.
+Preserve service errors, rejected code, authority denial, cancellation and limit
+exhaustion as distinct outcomes; do not report a successful candidate on stop.
+
+The full behavior and tests are in
+[reflection architecture](../../../etas-frontend/docs/architect/etas-reflection-design.md).

+### 14.1.1 Approval On Run And Checkpoint Resume
+
+The normative [run-scoped approval policy](../../../etas-core/docs/architect/etas-residual-checks-design.md#33-run-scoped-approval-and-explicit-reuse)
+replaces any assumption that saving execution state saves authorization.
+
+- A root run owns an in-memory approval registry. Bind evidence to that run,
+  action/input and applicable scope; expire it on Completed, Failed or Cancelled.
+  A child task/flow call does not create a new root run or widen approval scope.
+- Every checkpoint resume is a new run, even in one process. Use current options/
+  authority, but do not blindly reuse approval records in cloned options or a
+  previous context. New TraceId/request counters alone cannot enforce lifetime.
+- Restored historical decisions/results are data, not current grants. Native
+  restore rebinds approval evidence to unavailable and clears only its readiness
+  contribution; old Approved/armed flags cannot permit an action. Preserve all
+  unrelated progress, rejection/OR-branch history, cursors and completed work.
+- If further work requires approval, execute a new explicit application/source/
+  handler approval protocol at a checked safe continuation. Without one, reject
+  restoration or stop before that action with an accurate missing-current-
+  approval diagnostic. No automatic Approval.request, arbitrary source rewind,
+  silent skip or replay of completed external side effects is allowed.
+- Taking a checkpoint in a live run, normal suspension/yield and handler
+  continuation `resume` do not themselves expire a still-valid run approval.
+  Distinguish those operations from the checkpoint resume entry API.
+
+Static proof of approval order is conditional on its evidence lifetime. Planning
+and resume must retain that dependency even for a statically proven trace clause:
+starting at A in a new run cannot inherit the approval in `G; checkpoint; A`.
+Require an evidence-aware resume gate or reject safely; an empty residual set
+is not permission to discard this precondition.
+
+Implementation responsibility stays in existing layers:
+
+| Boundary | Responsibility |
+| --- | --- |
+| driver/lifecycle/{prepare,run,shutdown,resume}.rs and resume/source.rs | Create/end run ownership, use current authority and validate restore transitions |
+| eval/residual/{scope,evidence}.rs and control/residual/ | Run-bound evidence/readiness and permits; preserved historical monitor progress |
+| driver/dispatch/{approval,policy,host_dispatch}.rs and eval/boundary_approval.rs | Validate live responses, reject late/cross-run grants; historical ledger replay cannot mint current evidence |
+| api/codec/checkpoint/ and eval/machine/snapshot/ | Encode historical facts/explicit lifetime policy, never a trusted serialized grant; reject malformed/unsafe restoration |
+| host/services.rs and application service composition | Optional explicit approval-reuse provider and verification under current bindings |
+
+Only an application explicitly enabling cross-run reuse may supply persisted
+references for verification of issuer, decision, principal, scope mapping, input/
+resource, validity and applicable revocation. Import verified evidence into the
+new run within current authority; failure returns no permission. A checkpoint
+cannot choose this mode/provider. The application owns its durable backend and
+retention; the default runtime requires no approval database, signing key or
+generic trusted checkpoint store. Approval audit logs never keep grants alive.
+This rule applies equally to ordinary code and compiled Agent/Flow revisions.
+
